description: The default brand of Dense data: its theme picks in each mode. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

default.label: Dense data
default.description: The single brand: precise blue on cool grey.

theme.$description: The Dense data theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand color so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are violet, blue, green, amber, slate: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral slate.

open-ds.why: radius.2: We use a 2px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls and keep density. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough to read as an object, while it keeps straight lines that align in rows. So a dense toolbar reads as one line of actions, because the product is dense (content.q2) and precise (brand.q1), with slightly rounded controls (shape.values).

radius.0: We use a square corner for badges in order to give status a role of its own, apart from the 2px controls. A zero radius does this by keeping the badge a plain rectangle with no curve. So status badges line up down a table column, because badges get their own corner (shape.roles) and people scan and compare rows (tasks.q1).

radius.0: We use a square corner for menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 4px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance, and here no curve is left. So an option's edge runs parallel to its menu's edge, because surfaces take 4px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the layout is compact (spacing.values).

radius.2: We use the 2px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list row or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So rows and fields read as one family, because the control corner is small, not a pill (shape.values), and the product is dense (content.q2).

radius.4: We use a 4px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make touching panels read as separate objects, in a precise tone by brand convention. A small radius does this by breaking the outline at each corner, just softer than the 2px controls. So panels read apart yet still tile neatly, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is precise (brand.q1).

shadow.none: We use no shadow for cards in order to keep them at the page's height: on the scale only floating layers rise. The missing shade does this by leaving the card flat, framed by its line. So the page reads as one flat grid, because only menus and dialogs float (elevation.roles) and shadows are subtle (elevation.values).

shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by an 8px offset and a 24px blur at 16% under the panel's edge. So a menu reads as above the grid without a heavy edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are subtle (elevation.values).

The step does this by its place on the scheme's strong-ease curve, which spaces the dark steps by contrast. So a table header reads as recessed even on the page itself, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
neutral.0, under content: 1.1:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 16.26:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.

neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for parts that rise inside the page in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.25:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. Menus, dialogs and other floating layers take the next step up (surface.floating). So experts see what rises inside the page by its tone, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.150: We use one step lighter than raised for menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts in dark, in order to show that they float above everything else, 1.12:1 on surface.raised. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule, and keeps what sits on it readable: body text reads 11.64:1, muted text 4.63:1, and dividers and the ring stay lighter at 1.3:1. So experts read a menu as well as the page under it, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.15:1 under content and 1.05:1 under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on the surfaces it meets: 1.15:1 on surface.default, 1.44:1 on surface.raised and 1.61:1 on surface.floating, and 1.05:1 off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised and floating layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 7.46:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

neutral.floor: We use the highlight's step for a pressed item in dark in order to keep press and hover one state. The fill does this by staying where the hover put it. So experts get one plain signal and nothing more to learn, because the states are hover, focus and disabled, with no pressed look of its own (accessibility.roles), and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
